newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slip at open.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slip at open.

text.p: Singapore shares fell at the open on Friday as dealers sold down a range of blue chips ahead of the weekend.
Much of the early volume was in new issues with the latest listing, gold and fashion retailer Second Chance, doubling its initial public offer price in the first few minutes of trading.
The stock reached a high of Singapore $0.60, up from its S$0.30 issue price, and then slipped back to around S$0.56.
The 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) stood at 2,232.17 by 0130 GMT, down 16.17 points. Volume was a low 50 million shares with almost half of that in Second Chance.
A total of 25 stocks rose with 97 falling.
Among the gainers was sound-card maker Creative Technology, which put on a further 20 cents to S$17.20 as investors continued to adjust upwards their assessments of the electronics sector.

Another high technology stock to rally was telecommunications equipment company Datacraft Asia, which reported a 75 percent rise in first-half net profit on Thursday and predicted more growth for the full-year.
